brief: GS's Munaim opens with inflation's political salience: cost-of-living was the top issue in the just-concluded US midterms, consistent with recent CPI data and his own anecdotes (a $1800/night Legoland hotel room, flights almost 40% pricier a day earlier, both nearly sold out). GS's economics team responds: October CPI surprised meaningfully to the upside across categories, a third straight month of worse inflation news, so GS continues to expect a second 25bp hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike to its forecast, now placed in March 2027 rather than January, because it expects softer November/December prints followed by larger start-of-year price increases that lift January inflation. In FX, the post-midterm move barely touched currencies until the CPI surprise drove USD buying across the board, though a mid-week holiday and cautious positioning muted the flows. Long-JPY positioning partly unwound, giving holders of it as an AI-equity hedge room to add via options plus protection buying. Colleague Matt Atherton argues policy divergence, not growth shocks, now drives FX vol, with US data exceptionalism showing resilience to higher rates; GS likes USD calls against CHF into year-end and against EUR into the French election, the latter also hedging Middle East re-escalation risk.
